sections.title: Words Concatenation (hard)
sections.html:
Given a string and a list of words, find all the starting indices of substrings in the given string that are a concatenation of all the given words exactly once without any overlapping of words. It is given that all words are of the same length.

sections.title: Solution
sections.html:
This problem follows the Sliding Window pattern and has a lot of similarities with Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K. We will keep track of all the words in a HashMap and try to match them in the given string. Here are the set of steps for our algorithm:

  1. Keep the frequency of every word in a HashMap.
  2. Starting from every index in the string, try to match all the words.
  3. In each iteration, keep track of all the words that we have already seen in another HashMap.
  4. If a word is not found or has a higher frequency than required, we can move on to the next character in the string.
  5. Store the index if we have found all the words.

sections.title: Time Complexity
sections.html: The time complexity of the above algorithm will be O(N∗M∗Len)O(N * M * Len)O(N∗M∗Len) where ‘N’ is the number of characters in the given string, ‘M’ is the total number of words, and ‘Len’ is the length of a word.

sections.title: Space Complexity
sections.html: The space complexity of the algorithm is O(M)O(M)O(M) since at most, we will be storing all the words in the two HashMaps. In the worst case, we also need O(N)O(N)O(N) space for the resulting list. So, the overall space complexity of the algorithm will be O(M+N).O(M+N).O(M+N).
